about: Every version of the instructions a model is given in the pipeline, and its state (decisions 147.a, 148.a). A new version starts as a prototype: frozen and hashed beside the active one (frozen_contract.json holds its sha256), run only on chosen pages, its results kept apart and never served. It becomes active only by a person's decision after its gate, written before the run; the version it replaces is then retired, never deleted. One version per role is active. `parts` names what each file of a version is: the reader's rules, the reader's output format, the judge's instructions, the class check's. Each version names its origin (#17): who wrote it, a person, a model or a vendor, on which day, from which source, and how that is known; what cannot be known stays null, which says so. An origin that names a model as an author is kept on this machine only (`_work/prompt_origins.json`, the operator's 23.a), and the view shows it there.

parts.rules: Reader: what to transcribe and how faithfully, the blocks and their classes
parts.format: Format: the page file the reader writes, Markdown blocks with YAML front matter
parts.judge: Judge: how a model compares a reading with the page image, and what counts as a finding
parts.classcheck: Class check: a cheap model names which classes a page holds, before any reading is bought
parts.correction: Correction: a model proposes how one block should read, from the page image and a judge's finding, for a person to record or not
parts.task: Task: a document model's own instruction, as its vendor gives it (test readings)
parts.agent: Agent: how a Claude Code session starts the agent that reads or judges, around the reader's or the judge's own prompt

versions.title: A minimal correction of one block, the judge's finding a pointer
versions.why: The operator's W2.a (21 Nov): a person correcting a block from a judge's finding writes the block by hand; a model may propose it. It sees the page image, the block and every finding on it, takes the finding as a pointer to check in the image, never as a fact, and changes as little as it can. Its gate, written before the run: the person corrections whose block carries a finding the person rated right or right for a wrong reason (14 on 21 Nov, in both pipeline databases). Per case the person's edit and the proposal's edit, as words added and removed against the reading: a case passes with edit recall at least 0.8 and edit precision at least 0.6, or, for a description a person worded their own way, where line 1 reads that the proposal corrects every fact the person corrected and adds no error (listed by name). It passes with at least 11 of the 14, at least 2 of the 4 rated right for a wrong reason among them, so a judge's wrong evidence is not followed. The three false alarms and the one case without a rating are reported beside it. At most 0.60 USD. → now (run 21 Nov, 0.27 USD): failed, 8 of 14 (6 by words, 2 descriptions by line 1's reading: a swap of two values the word measure cannot see, and a fact worded otherwise), 1 of the rated right for a wrong reason, of which there are 3, not 4 as the gate said. The misses: three empty tables written as pipe tables, one with a header the page does not print (its own format line named |); a chart's crossing read as 2010 where the person read 2012; a value -9.5 where the person read -10; an unclear mark dropped where the person kept it.

versions.title: correction/1 + tables as HTML, inline marks kept, chart values at the axis
versions.why: correction/1's misses, each a rule: a table is HTML inside its block, never with a header the page does not print; the transcription's inline marks are kept, an unclear one too, the likelier reading first; a chart's value is read against the axis at the exact point, a crossing where the lines meet. Its gate, written before the run: the same 14 cases, 11 rated right and 3 right for a wrong reason; a case passes with edit recall at least 0.8 and edit precision at least 0.6, or, for a description or a swap of values the word measure cannot see, where line 1 reads that the proposal corrects every fact the person corrected and adds no error (listed by name). It passes with at least 11 of the 14 and 2 of the 3. At most 0.60 USD. → now (run 21 Nov, 0.27 USD): passed, 13 of 14 (11 by words, 2 descriptions by line 1's reading: a swap of two values, a fact worded otherwise), 2 of the 3; an unclear time cell came back exactly as the person wrote it. The miss: a chart's crossing the person read as 2012, the proposal as 2008 to 2010 (the judge's wrong 2006 to 2007 not followed). Beside the gate, on the three false alarms the proposal agreed with the judge at least in part each time, so a proposal never replaces a person's look at the image. → now, the same instructions on claude-opus-5-5 (the operator's A1.b, 21 Nov, 0.54 USD): 12 of 14, 2 of the 3. It read the chart's crossing as the person did (2012), which Sonnet, the reader's and the judge's model, missed; it kept the unclear time cell's first reading where the person put the other first (the word measure counts that a pass, being a swap; read, it is a miss), and read one chart value -9.5 where the person read -10. On the page without a finding it changed nothing and said so. → now, on 11 open issues without a person's verdict (the operator's C1.a, 21 Nov, 0.47 USD for both models), each proposal read by line 1 against the page image: Opus 9 of 11, Sonnet 6 of 11. The open issues held 4 false alarms of the judge (a chart value read right, an order's bars told from the volume's, an order count that is there, a formula that matches); Opus left all four as they were, Sonnet followed the judge on two and rewrote a third. Opus read an event graph's initializing arrows right where Sonnet did not. Both followed the judge on one chart value (0.35 read as 0.3) and missed the order of a blurred screenshot's axis labels. → now active, on claude-opus-5-5 (the operator's M1.b, 21 Nov), the model the configuration names.
